from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Define epsilon for target accuracy.",
            "Define delta for input range.",
            "Does delta force epsilon bounds?",
            "The box trap proves it.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Formal Rigor: Epsilon-Delta Definition", lecture_lines)

        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 4], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)

        epsilon_val = 0.5
        delta_val = 0.6
        c = 1.0
        L = 1.0
        
        # Using SVG for the Epsilon-box
        box_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg"
        epsilon_rect = SVGMobject(box_path, color="#FFFF00")
        epsilon_rect.set_width(1.5)
        epsilon_rect.move_to(axes.c2p(c, L))
        
        # Delta interval
        delta_line = Line(axes.c2p(c - delta_val, -0.1), axes.c2p(c + delta_val, -0.1), color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Labels
        eps_label = Text("Epsilon", font_size=18, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eps_label, 'C1', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        del_label = Text("Delta", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(del_label, 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(epsilon_rect))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(delta_line))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))

outline.topic: Mastering Limits: From Intuition to Precision and Shortcuts

sections.title: The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach
sections.content: Introduce the limit as a 'trend' rather than a destination. Use a rabbit hopping toward a carrot; the rabbit gets infinitely close to the carrot (the limit) but never 'becomes' the carrot. Define the limit as the value a function approaches as x approaches a point c.
sections.example: A rabbit jumping toward a fence at x=2. Even if the ground at x=2 is missing (a hole), the rabbit knows exactly where it's headed.

sections.title: The Formal Rigor: Epsilon-Delta Definition (The Bodyguard Logic)
sections.content: Transition to formal definitions. Explain the 'Epsilon-Delta' game: If you want to get within a tiny distance (epsilon) of the target value L, can I find a distance (delta) around c that forces the function to stay within your goal? Visually, represent this as a shrinking box trap.
sections.example: A bodyguard (delta) ensures a celebrity (the function value) stays within a specific crowd fence (epsilon) as they walk toward the stage (x=c).

sections.title: The Computational Shortcut: L'Hôpital's Rule
sections.content: Introduce L'Hôpital's Rule for indeterminate forms (0/0). Explain that when a function is too complex to 'see' the limit, we compare their 'growth speeds' (derivatives) instead. Emphasize that this is like looking at the slopes of two competing racecars at the starting line.
sections.example: Comparing a fast-accelerating rocket (f(x)) and a slow-rising elevator (g(x)) as they both approach an 'indeterminate' starting gate at x=0.

sections.title: Synthesis & Visual Summary
sections.content: Briefly recap the journey: We moved from the rabbit's intuition (Concept), to the bodyguard's precision (Definition), to the rocket's acceleration (L'Hôpital). Provide a final visual flow chart showing when to use which tool.
sections.example: A 'Limit Toolbox' graphic: Use the Epsilon-Delta trap for proofs, and L'Hôpital's rocket fuel for quick calculation of complex fractions.
